newsitem.title: USA: Stella stock sales by 10 agents halted.
newsitem.headline: Stella stock sales by 10 agents halted.

text.p: New York State Attorney General Dennis Vacco said Tuesday he had obtained a preliminary restraining order stopping 10 Russian nationals from selling stock in Stella Bella Corp, an operator of coffee houses.
Vacco alleged that the 10 Russians, all men, were running an illegal telemarketing campaign aimed at cheating hundreds of senior citizens.
He said the 10 sold the stock through a New York-based company called Z3 Capital Corp. He said the 10 agents were unregistered, untrained and unsupervised.
The restraining order was issued Friday by a New York State Supreme Court judge, Vacco said.

He said the agents contacted investors through unsolicited phone calls and used high-pressure sales techniques and false information to lure them to buy stock. Most of the investors were senior citizens living on fixed incomes.
Many investors purchased Stella Bella stock for around $1 a share, he said. It is now trading at about $0.23.

He alleged that investors were told the stock price would triple within months, that they could purchase the securities at below the market price, and that President Clinton's brother-in-law was to be an integral part of Stella Bella.
Investors were also told that if their investments went bad, all their money would be returned, he alleged.
